ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma

salient_findings: Confluent lichenified erythromelanotic plaques with overlying thick greasy scales
Superficial dermal band-like lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal fibrosis
key_facts: Previous treatment with oral prednisolone and cyclosporine without improvement
Skin punch biopsies showed epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes
Immunohistochemical staining showed tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO
Negative direct immunofluorescence for fibrinogen, C3, IgA, IgM, and IgG

shortlist: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes and dermal fibrosis are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Erythroderma and presence of atypical lymphocytes in skin biopsies are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical staining showed tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO, consistent with T-cell origin

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Epidermotropism and CD8 negativity are not typical, but CD3 positivity and aggressive nature make it a consideration

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma can present with erythroderma and epidermotropism, although CD3 and CD45RO positivity is more typical of alpha/beta T-cells

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically presents with papular lesions, lymphomatoid papulosis can have a wide range of clinical presentations, including erythroderma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to primary cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma, but with a more aggressive course

shortlist.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to lack of systemic symptoms and negative direct immunofluorescence, the presence of atypical lymphocytes and dermal fibrosis make it a consideration

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of erythroderma, epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes, and immunohistochemical staining showing tumor cells positive for CD3 and CD45RO but negative for CD4, CD8, and CD7 are consistent with mycosis fungoides, particularly the epidermotropic pattern and the lack of specific markers for other conditions.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome typically presents with more systemic involvement and lymphadenopathy, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical staining did not show positivity for CD8, which is characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The staining pattern does not support gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma, as it would typically be negative for CD3 and CD45RO or show a different immunophenotype.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides; the specific details point more precisely to mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid papulosis typically presents with a more acute, papular eruption rather than the confluent erythroderma seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Similar to primary cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma, the immunophenotype does not match.

rejected.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition is typically associated with HTLV-1 infection and has a distinct clinical presentation and immunophenotype that does not match the case details provided.
